A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same augmented equilibrium propagation study. All 12 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 experiments, including classification accuracy, memory consumption, training dynamics, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds diagnostic evidence about neuron-state perturbations and convergence failure in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The three-phase EP procedure, local-error and knowledge-distillation losses, weighted-distillation extension, and signal schedulers remain unchanged. The mapping-update equations move from v1 Appendix G into v2 Section 4.3; this is not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image-classification coverage. The additional convergence diagnostics concern retained architectures and tasks, without introducing another dataset, population, or input environment.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same VGG-5 comparators from Laborieux et al. (2021), Laydevant et al. (2021), and Laborieux and Zenke (2022). Tables 2–3 retain standard EP, BPTT, and KD/KDW comparisons. Newly cited residual-connection approaches are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds an extended-duration convergence check with Tfree = 1000 and Tnudge = 400. Figure 5 changes its reported aggregation to mean absolute activations per neuron and gradients per parameter, replacing v1's captioned mean activations and summed gradients. Main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A extends the existing vanishing-gradient analysis with Figure 5e, directly comparing free and nudged states, and reports initialization and longer-simulation checks. These examine alternative explanations for convergence failure. The scheduler and weighted-distillation ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs with standard deviations below 0.4 in Table 1 and below 0.3 in Table 3. Figure 3 retains standard-deviation shading over 100 samples, and Appendix D retains the statement that random seeds are not manually set.

E6.justification: Figure 5 reports revised normalized values and adds minimal free-versus-nudged state differences. Appendix A newly reports convergence failure despite extended simulation. Tables 1–3 are unchanged, including 89.67% CIFAR-10 accuracy for VGG-7-KD and 64.75% CIFAR-100 accuracy for VGG-12-KD; the revised diagnostics do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 replaces convergence asserted from continuous differentiability with explicit assumptions of a contractive base map, Lipschitz loss gradients, and K1 + |beta|K2 + |beta*kappa|K3 < 1. The proof, moved from Appendix F to G, adds the contraction requirement and uniqueness conclusion. Equation 6 also changes the EP/BPTT sign. These materially revise the formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The novelty, deeper-network scalability, and CIFAR state-of-the-art claims remain. The abstract narrows its concluding implication from enabling real-world applications to extending EP to deeper architectures, while the Discussion qualifies scalability as applying to the framework considered here.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds explanations for the U-shaped gradient profile and attributes subsequent state decay to small gradients combined with weight decay. The Discussion adds an argument that stored teacher signals permit local on-chip KD learning and discusses hardware implementation of LE. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-repository link and explicit signaling-layer index rows in Tables 5–6, but removes their hyperparameter Range columns. Selected hyperparameters, teacher specifications, hardware, and software disclosures otherwise remain. The new index rows document settings rather than establish that experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu and Chen (2025) to the residual-connection discussion and acknowledges independent work by Elayedam and Srinivasan (2025), positioning their architectural approach as complementary to intermediate signaling. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted prose revisions, expands Appendix A and the Discussion, renames Section 3.2, and moves mapping-update material into Section 4.3. It adds an appendix explaining standard mathematical operators and an acknowledgments section. Most wording and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column formatting, with restyled headings, author information, captions, and repositioned tables and figures. Figure 5 changes from four vertically stacked panels to a five-panel arrangement with revised axes. Tables 5–6 also change their row and column structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves rigor by stating essential contraction conditions in Theorem 3.1 and strengthening the vanishing-gradient diagnosis with direct state comparisons and an extended-duration control. These support the existing contribution more clearly. Gains are limited by removal of hyperparameter ranges and remaining inconsistency between the theorem's loss-gradient Lipschitz assumptions and Appendix G's loss-Lipschitz wording.
